Executive Order 13668 of May 27, 2014 
Ending Immunities Granted to the Development Fund for 
Iraq and Certain Other Iraqi Property and Interests in Prop-
erty Pursuant to Executive Order 13303, as Amended 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including the International Emergency 
Economic Powers Act, as amended (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.) (IEEPA), the 
National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.), section 5 of the United 
Nations Participation Act, as amended (22 U.S.C. 287c) (UNPA), and section 
301 of title 3, United States Code, 
I, BARACK OBAMA, President of the United States of America, have deter-
mined that the situation that gave rise to the actions taken in Executive 
Order 13303 of May 22, 2003, to protect the Development Fund for Iraq 
and certain other property in which the Government of Iraq has an interest 
has been significantly altered. Recognizing the changed circumstances in 
Iraq, including the Government of Iraq’s progress in resolving and managing 
the risk associated with outstanding debts and claims arising from actions 
of the previous regime, I hereby terminate the prohibitions contained in 
section 1 of Executive Order 13303 of May 22, 2003, as amended by Executive 
Order 13364 of November 29, 2004, on any attachment, judgment, decree, 
lien, execution, garnishment, or other judicial process with respect to the 
Development Fund for Iraq and Iraqi petroleum, petroleum products, and 
interests therein, and the accounts, assets, investments, and other property 
owned by, belonging to, or held by, in the name of, on behalf of, or otherwise 
for, the Central Bank of Iraq. This action is not intended otherwise to 
affect the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13303 of May 
22, 2003, as expanded in scope by Executive Order 13315 of August 28, 
2003, which shall remain in place. This action is also not intended to 
affect immunities enjoyed by the Government of Iraq and its property under 
otherwise applicable law. 
I hereby order: 
Section 1. The prohibitions set forth in section 1 of Executive Order 13303 
of May 22, 2003, as amended by Executive Order 13364 of November 29, 
2004, are hereby terminated. 
Sec. 2. The Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary 
of State, is hereby authorized to take such actions, including the promulgation 
of rules and regulations, and to employ all powers granted to the President 
by IEEPA and the UNPA as may be necessary to carry out the purposes 
of this order. The Secretary of the Treasury may redelegate any of these 
functions to other officers and agencies of the United States Government. 
All agencies of the United States Government are hereby directed to take 
all appropriate measures within their statutory authority to carry out the 
provisions of this order.

research_rationale:
The held official Federal Register text of EO 13303 (68 FR 31931, FR Doc. 03-13412, published 2003-05-28) was read in full. It declares a national emergency over the threat of judicial process against the Development Fund for Iraq and Iraqi petroleum, prohibits attachment and similar process against them (sec. 1), carves the property out of EOs 12722, 12724 and 13290 (sec. 2), defines terms (sec. 3), authorises the Treasury to implement (sec. 4) and has the usual disclaimers. The 16-clause inventory covers the opening paragraphs, each section and each lettered definition and was confirmed against the text. Sec. 1 and its subsections ended on 2014-05-27 when EO 13668 terminated the sec. 1 prohibitions as amended by EO 13364, a termination that by its own words left the national emergency in place. The emergency is continued each May by a notice: all 23 notices from 2004 to 2026 are held and attached as later events to the lead clause, the last signed 2026-05-04, which carries the emergency past 2026-05-22 and so through 2026-10-14. The Office of the Federal Register catalogue lists the order as amended by EO 13364 with no revocation. The U.S. Code search covers editions current through 2026-10-09, so a law enacted from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 is not reflected. The authority statutes (IEEPA, the National Emergencies Act, the United Nations Participation Act) are cited in the order and referred to in the 2026 notice as the basis of the continued emergency; no held source shows any of them repealed or expired.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 13303 has no savings clause of its own. Its sec. 2(b) preserves administrative action taken under EOs 12722, 12724 and 13290 or under IEEPA and the UNPA. dent’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, and in order to change the name 
of the ‘‘President’s Committee on Mental Retardation’’ to the ‘‘President’s 
Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities’’ (the ‘‘Committee’’) and 
expand the membership of the Committee, it is hereby ordered as follows:

named the President’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities.

deleting the words ‘‘mental retardation’’ and inserting the words ‘‘intellectual 
disabilities’’ in lieu thereof throughout the text of that order, except in 
the title, the first line of the preamble, and section 1 of that order.

through (13).

W

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sec. 3 amends section 1 of EO 12994 by deleting the words "(the ‘‘Committee’’)" and adding after "responsibilities," the words naming the renamed committee. Its effect is that sec. 1 of EO 12994 calls the body the President’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities. No end is stated. EO 13446 sec. 5 restated sec. 1 of EO 12994 with the same sentence, "The President’s Committee on Mental Retardation, with expanded membership and expanded responsibilities, and renamed the President’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities (Committee), is hereby continued in operation", and the 42 U.S.C. 15001 note prints that text as current EO 12994 as amended by EO 13309. Before the restatement this clause supplied the words; after it the restated section carries the same words. EO 13446 sec. 5 (signed 2007-09-28, "This order shall be effective September 30, 2007.") further amended EO 12994 "to read as follows", restating the whole of EO 12994; under the owner ruling on strike-and-insert and restatement amendments (2026-10-21) this clause continues, amended, and the restatement is a later event; the reviewer should note that the restatement replaced the text of EO 12994 and changed the wording of this clause's subject.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sec. 5 says "The Committee is continued until September 30, 2005." The date is the stated end of this command and is recorded inclusive (the continuance runs through the end of 2005-09-30); on the exclusive reading it ended when that day began. Nothing in the order extends it. The committee was later continued by separate orders each with its own date and terms; EO 13446 sec. 1(g) (signed 2007-09-28, effective 2007-09-30) lists "President’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities; Executive Order 12994, as amended" among the committees "continued until September 30, 2009", which is a new continuance by a later order and not an extension of this clause, which is why this clause is recorded as terminated on its own stated date while the committee itself continues under other commands.

research_rationale:
The held official Federal Register text (68 FR 44851, FR Doc. 03-19572, filed 2003-07-30) was read in full and is the order signed 2003-07-25 by President Bush: its heading is Executive Order 13309 of July 25, 2003, and its five sections rename the President’s Committee on Mental Retardation, amend EO 12994 and continue the committee until 2005-09-30. The clause inventory of five sections was confirmed against the text and covers every operative sentence. Sections 1 to 4 are amending commands whose results are carried in the current text of EO 12994, which the 42 U.S.C. 15001 note (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints as amended by EO 13309 and EO 13446 sec. 5; EO 13446 restated EO 12994 effective 2007-09-30 and is attached as a later event to each of those clauses. Section 5 ended on its own stated date. The bounded searches named below (U.S. Code, eCFR and the Office of the Federal Register catalogue) were read for coverage: the U.S. Code search covers editions current through 2026-10-09, so a law enacted from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 is not reflected; the catalogue and the number search of the held texts found no revocation, supersession or further amendment of EO 13309 itself.

Executive Order 13309 of July 25, 2003
Amendments to Executive Order 12994, and Renaming the 
President’s Committee on Mental Retardation as the Presi-
dent’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, and in order to change the name 
of the ‘‘President’s Committee on Mental Retardation’’ to the ‘‘President’s 
Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities’’ (the ‘‘Committee’’) and 
expand the membership of the Committee, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. The President’s Committee on Mental Retardation is hereby re-
named the President’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities. 
Sec. 2. Executive Order 12994 of March 21, 1996, is hereby amended by 
deleting the words ‘‘mental retardation’’ and inserting the words ‘‘intellectual 
disabilities’’ in lieu thereof throughout the text of that order, except in 
the title, the first line of the preamble, and section 1 of that order. 
Sec. 3. Section 1 of Executive Order 12994 is amended by deleting the 
words ‘‘(the ‘‘Committee’’)’’ and adding after ‘‘responsibilities,’’ the words 
‘‘and renamed the President’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabil-
ities (the ‘‘Committee’’),’’. 
Sec. 4. Section 2 of Executive Order 12994 is amended by inserting after 
‘‘(5) The Secretary of Housing and Urban Development;’’ the following: 
‘‘(6) The Secretary of Commerce; (7) The Secretary of Transportation; (8) 
The Secretary of the Interior; (9) The Secretary of Homeland Security;’’ 
and renumbering former subsections (6) through (9) as subsections (10) 
through (13). 
Sec. 5. The Committee is continued until September 30, 2005.
W
THE WHITE HOUSE, 
July 25, 2003.
